answer: Freddie Mac is the original source. It publishes the rate weekly, as of each Thursday, through its Primary Mortgage Market Survey. The series is in percent, not seasonally adjusted, and runs from 1971-04-02 to 2026-10-01 (latest observation). Since November 17, 2022, Freddie Mac has based the survey on applications lenders submit to it. Source: Freddie Mac via FRED series MORTGAGE30US.

The source is S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC. FRED's copy holds only 10 years of daily closing values, because of its licensing agreement with S&P DJI. As of 2026-10-06 it runs from 2016-10-06 to 2026-10-05. It is a price index, so dividends are not included, and it is not seasonally adjusted. Source: S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC via FRED series SP500.

The source is S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC. FRED's title is now 'S&P Cotality Case-Shiller U.S. National Home Price Index' (Cotality was formerly CoreLogic). It is monthly, with units of Index Jan 2000=100 and no seasonal adjustment, and runs from January 1987 to July 2026. Source: S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC via FRED series CSUSHPINSA.

It comes from the University of Michigan's Surveys of Consumers. The series is monthly, with units of Index 1966:Q1=100 and no seasonal adjustment. At the source's request FRED shows it one month late, so the latest observation is August 2026. Data before January 1978 are in series UMCSENT1. Source: University of Michigan via FRED series UMCSENT.

The source is the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), in its Spot Prices release. The series is the daily WTI spot price at Cushing, Oklahoma, in dollars per barrel and not seasonally adjusted. It runs from 1986-01-02 to 2026-09-29. Source: U.S. EIA via FRED series DCOILWTICO.

The source is the U.S. Department of Labor's Employment and Training Administration, in its Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims Report. Yes, the headline series is seasonally adjusted. It is weekly, for weeks ending Saturday, measured as a number of claims, and runs from 1967 to the week ending 2026-09-26. Source: U.S. Employment and Training Administration via FRED series ICSA.

Real GDP on FRED is in billions of chained 2017 dollars, at a seasonally adjusted annual rate. The series is quarterly and runs from Q1 1947 to Q2 2026. Source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis via FRED series GDPC1.

The units are an index with base period 1982-1984=100. The headline series is seasonally adjusted and monthly, running from January 1947 to August 2026. Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics via FRED series CPIAUCSL.

The U.S. Census Bureau and the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development publish it jointly, in the New Residential Sales release. FRED's metadata titles the series 'Median Sales Price of New Houses Sold for the United States'. It is quarterly, in dollars and not seasonally adjusted, and runs from Q1 1963 to Q2 2026. Source: U.S. Census Bureau and HUD via FRED series MSPUS.

The Federal Reserve Bank of New York is the source of the daily Effective Federal Funds Rate. It is a volume-weighted median of overnight federal funds trades reported on the FR 2420 report. The series is in percent and not seasonally adjusted, and runs from 2000-07-03 to 2026-10-02. Source: Federal Reserve Bank of New York via FRED series EFFR. I could not check the source of the monthly FEDFUNDS or daily DFF series, because the connector intermittently returned HTTP 403. My understanding, not from FRED, is that those two are credited to the Federal Reserve Board of Governors.
